paper_metadata.title: The Lie Algebra of XY-mixer Topologies and Warm Starting QAOA for Constrained Optimization

experiments.description: Multi-angle QAOA with warm-starting on portfolio optimization instances from the S&P 500, evaluated across multiple problem sizes and depths.

algorithm.ansatz: XY-mixer cycle with RZ phase separators; full circuit adds RZZ gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 100 steps in the restricted circuit, then 100 steps in the full circuit; performance reported over p-depths up to 40

hyperparameters.warm_start_transfer: RZ and XY-mixer parameters transferred; RZZ parameters initialized to 0
hyperparameters.phase_separators: GZ in restricted circuit; GZ,ZZ in full circuit

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random uniform in [0, 2π] for restricted circuit; transferred learned parameters to full circuit with RZZ angles set to zero

problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x -p^T x + q x^T C x subject to |x| = k
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: XY-mixer preserves Hamming weight; cardinality constraint enforced by Dicke-state initialization and symmetry-preserving mixer
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_f = H_p + q H_covar, where H_p = -∑_i p_i σ_i^1 and H_covar = ∑_{i,j} C_{ij} σ_i^1 σ_j^1

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on monthly S&P 500 instances

dataset_specification.description: 84 monthly instances from 2010 to 2018; top-performing stocks selected by average monthly return; returns vector and covariance matrix constructed from historical price data; target portfolio size k = n/2

quantum_resources.num_variational_params: 2np for warm-start restricted circuit; (n^2 + 3n)p/2 for full circuit

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute expected returns and covariance matrix from monthly S&P 500 price data; select top n assets; formulate portfolio objective and constraint
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate approximation ratio and success probability from final state

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical runtime or asymptotic speedup comparison is reported; the paper compares warm-started vs random initialization within QAOA.

experiments.description: Shared-angle QAOA versus multi-angle QAOA on portfolio optimization, with and without warm-starting.

algorithm.variant: shared-angle QAOA vs multi-angle QAOA, both with warm-start and random initialization
algorithm.ansatz: SA-QAOA uses shared angles per layer; MA-QAOA uses individually parameterized gates; both use XY-mixer and Z-based phase separators
algorithm.convergence_criteria: performance compared across p-depths up to 40; warm-start pretraining uses 100 steps and refinement uses 100 steps

hyperparameters.warm_start_transfer: learned restricted parameters transferred to full circuit; RZZ angles initialized to 0 in MA-QAOA full circuit

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random uniform in [0, 2π] for restricted circuits; warm-start transfer to full circuits; random starts used as baseline

problem_formulation.objective_function: portfolio optimization: min_x -p^T x + q x^T C x subject to |x| = k
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: XY-mixer and Dicke-state initialization enforce cardinality constraint

dataset_specification.description: 84 monthly instances from 2010 to 2018; top-performing stocks selected by average monthly return; k = n/2

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct returns vector and covariance matrix from monthly S&P 500 data; formulate constrained portfolio objective
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare approximation ratio and log success probability across SA-QAOA and MA-QAOA

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline is reported; comparison is between SA-QAOA and MA-QAOA, with and without warm-starting.

experiments.description: Warm-started multi-angle QAOA on graph partitioning instances.

algorithm.ansatz: XY-mixer cycle with RZ phase separators; full circuit includes RZZ gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 100 steps in the restricted circuit and 100 steps in the full circuit; results reported for p-depths up to 24
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random uniform in [0, 2π] for restricted circuit; learned parameters transferred to full circuit with RZZ angles set to 0

problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x (1 - x^T) A x subject to |x| = n/2
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_f = |E|/2 I + (1/2)∑_{i<j} Z_i Z_j for the min-cut formulation

dataset_specification.description: Random graphs with 2n edges and n vertices (Rnd(2n)) and 3-regular random graphs (3-Reg); evaluated for n = 12 and 14

quantum_resources.num_variational_params: 2np for restricted circuit; (n^2 + 3n)p/2 for full circuit

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate random graph instances (Rnd(2n) and 3-Reg); compute adjacency matrix and min-cut Hamiltonian
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate approximation ratio and log success probability over depth and training steps

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical optimization baseline is reported; the paper compares warm-started vs random-start QAOA on graph partitioning.

experiments.description: Warm-started multi-angle QAOA on sparsest k-subgraph instances.

algorithm.ansatz: XY-mixer cycle with RZ phase separators; full circuit includes RZZ gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 100 steps in the restricted circuit and 100 steps in the full circuit; results reported for p-depths up to 24
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random uniform in [0, 2π] for restricted circuit; learned parameters transferred to full circuit with RZZ angles set to 0

problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x x^T A x subject to |x| = n/2

dataset_specification.description: Random graphs with 2n edges and n vertices (Rnd(2n)) and 3-regular random graphs (3-Reg); evaluated for n = 12, 14, and 16

quantum_resources.num_variational_params: 2np for restricted circuit; (n^2 + 3n)p/2 for full circuit

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate random graph instances; compute adjacency matrix and sparsest-subgraph Hamiltonian
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate approximation ratio and log success probability over depth and training steps

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline is reported; the comparison is between warm-started and randomly initialized QAOA on synthetic graph instances.

experiments.description: Lie-algebraic analysis and numerical verification of XY-mixer circuit expressibility and warm-start restriction strategy; no separate end-user optimization benchmark beyond the QAOA experiments.

algorithm.variant: dynamical Lie algebra analysis of XY-mixer topologies

problem_instance.description: Theoretical/numerical DLA classification across XY-mixer topologies; not a standalone optimization benchmark

dataset_specification.description: Small-n numerical verification reported in Supplementary Table S2 for n = 3 to 9

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical simulation / training of circuits with exponential dynamical Lie algebras
speedup_claims.conditions: Polynomial-sized DLAs (e.g., cycle XY with RZ) are argued to be efficiently trainable; exponential DLAs (e.g., clique XY or inclusion of RZZ) are intractable to train classically
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a trainability/simulability argument, not an end-to-end runtime speedup benchmark.
